relevance_note: Case report of two boys with TNFAIP3 variants presenting with HLH ("we report two children with the primary presentation of HLH, with a mutation in TNFAIP3"), plus a literature table and text describing further individual HA20 / TNFAIP3 patients.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; values were typed into a Python builder script (scratch dir) that assembles the JSON and checks every span verbatim. No table was transcribed by script. Scope and labels: the two first-hand patients are labelled by their section headings 'Patient one' and 'Patient two' (the text also calls them 'our first/second patient'; Table 3 calls them 'Our patient N. 1' / 'Our patient N. 2' in rows 3 and 4, which are the same people, not extra rows). Patient two's parents were tested (WES and Sanger, 'homozygous wild type') and are in scope as tested-negative relatives; the paper never says mother/father, so they are labelled 'parent of Patient two' and 'parent of Patient two 2' with sex not reported and no variant rows. Out of scope: Patient one's parents ('son of two cousins') and healthy older sister, neither tested nor affected. Previously published people: Table 3 rows 1 (Li et al. [29]) and 2 (Takagi et al. [9]) are labelled by the table's 'Number' column ('1', '2'); the text descriptions of the same two people were merged into these rows. The three patients of Zhang et al. [25] described individually in the Discussion were given rows 'ref [25] patient', 'ref [25] patient 2', 'ref [25] patient 3'; the paper ties them to HA20 only by context and prints no TNFAIP3 variant for them, so they have no variant rows. Li et al.'s other three HA20 patients are mentioned only as a count and get no rows. Table 3 'Other features' cells marked '-' for our patients are not defined as absent in the legend, so they were not used. Group statements 'Our patients did not have any symptoms of Behcet's-like or other autoimmune disorders' and 'we did not find any positive autoantibodies ... in our patients' (both first-hand patients explicitly) were used as group-statement exclusions; the Behcet's-like statement was recorded as its own feature but not mapped to specific checklist items (oral/genital/GI ulcers, uveitis etc. left 'not reported'). Cytopenias in Patients one and two are attributed to HLH, not stated as autoimmune, so 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' is 'not reported'. Patient one 'central nervous system involvement' = observed on the basis of terminal cerebral hemorrhage with coma. 'Intermittent fever' was treated as recurrent fever; Patient two's single 'prolonged fever' was not. Age at diagnosis for Patient one is the age at which the WES result (HA20) was delivered (2 years 4 months); his HLH was diagnosed at 4 months; his age at death is not given. Patient two's age at genetic diagnosis is not stated as an age; 'At the time of writing this report, 4 years have passed since the first presentation' is a follow-up interval, not an age, so age at last evaluation was left 'not reported'. Takagi's TNFAIP3 variant is called 'de novo' but no parental testing is described, so inheritance = not reported (rule 8). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (the paper does not say either way). Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: (1) Patient two's protein change is described as 'a proline to leucine amino acid change (p. L275P)', but p.L275P denotes leucine to proline; both recorded as printed. (2) Patient one: the text says 'He had normal ESR, CRP, and procalcitonin levels', but Table 1 shows ESR 11 (range 0-10) and CRP 6 (range <6) without asterisks; recorded as excluded per the explicit statement. (3) Patient two: 'the coagulation profile was normal, except for thrombocytopenia', yet hypofibrinogenemia (fibrinogen 93*) is reported elsewhere; hypofibrinogenemia recorded as observed, no 'normal coagulation' row. (4) Patient two: 'leukocytosis and thrombocytosis were resolved' after etanercept, but no leukocytosis or thrombocytosis is shown in Table 2 (which shows leukopenia/thrombocytopenia before treatment); recorded as stated. (5) Patient one: the case section says the HLH 2004 criteria were met, while the Discussion says all five criteria might not have been met (hemoglobin 9.2 g/dl above the 9 g/dl threshold). (6) The Background says 'we present a case' although two are reported. (7) Li patient variant printed as 'c.C259T, p.R87X' in Table 3 and 'c.259C > T (p.R87X)' in the text; the text form (with transcript NM_006290) was recorded.
